accepted.label: a
accepted.text: In all parts, if more than 1 coordinate pair is offered then mark the "final" pair. Accept missing brackets as long as the intention is clear e.g. $-2, -3$ or $(-2, -3$

accepted.label: a
accepted.text: You may have to use your judgement to decide if the A1 conditions are satisfied. Example: f(2) = –3, f(3) = 41, there is a change of sign hence f(x) has a continuous root in [2, 3] Scores M1A0 – i.e. it is not the root that is continuous

accepted.label: b
accepted.text: Condone working backwards as long as there is a (minimal) conclusion e.g. $x=\sqrt[3]{\dfrac{5x^2-4x+7}{x}}\Rightarrow x^3=\dfrac{5x^2-4x+7}{x}\Rightarrow x^4-5x^2+4x-7=0$ ✓, #, QED, hence shown, etc.

accepted.label: b
accepted.text: Some candidates may attempt to differentiate the original f(x) e.g.: $f'(x)=\dfrac{4x(3x^2+7x-20)-(2x^2-32)(6x+7)}{(3x^2+7x-20)^2}-\dfrac{24}{(3x-5)^2}$ Score M1 for: $f'(x)=\dfrac{Ax(3x^2+7x-20)-(2x^2-32)(Cx+D)}{(3x^2+7x-20)^2}-\dfrac{E}{(3x-5)^2}$ and (first) A1 if they reach $\dfrac{-10}{(3x-5)^2}$

accepted.label: d
accepted.text: If you are unsure if the reasoning is acceptable or not, use review.

accepted.label: c
accepted.text: Note we are scoring the first mark as an M mark not a B mark.

accepted.label: a
accepted.text: A typical response with an expanded denominator: (a) $y=\dfrac{16}{9(3x-k)}=\dfrac{16}{27x-9k}\Rightarrow\dfrac{dy}{dx}=-\dfrac{432}{(27x-9k)^2}$ M1A0 (b) $-\dfrac{432}{(27x-9k)^2}=-12\Rightarrow12(27x-9k)^2=432$ M1 $12(27x-9k)^2=432\Rightarrow(27x-9k)^2=36\Rightarrow27-9k=\pm6\Rightarrow k=...$ dM1 $k=\dfrac{7}{3},\dfrac{11}{3}$ A1 (c) $y=\dfrac{16}{27-21}$ M1 (B1 on ePEN) $y-\text{"}\frac{8}{3}\text{"}=\dfrac{1}{12}(x-1)$ dM1 $12y-x-31=0$ A1 (d) $\int\dfrac{16}{27x-9k}dx=\dfrac{16}{27}[\ln(27x-9k)]$ M1 $=\dfrac{16}{27}[\ln(27x-21)]$ A1ft $\dfrac{16}{27}[\ln(27x-21)]_1^3=\dfrac{16}{27}(\ln(27(3)-21)-\ln(27-21))$ dM1 $=\dfrac{16}{27}\ln(10)$ A1

accepted.label: b
accepted.text: Do not condone poor squaring for this mark. e.g. do not condone $3\sin2x=2+4\cos2x\Rightarrow9\sin^22x=4+16\cos^22x$
